entry.title: When teeth begin to appear
entry.summary: The authors describe teething as easy for some babies and uncomfortable for others. Their account includes comfort and care for a newly emerged tooth, while their wider discussion keeps medical advice available for crying or pain.
entry.cue: You are noticing drool or caring for a tooth that has appeared.
detail: Keeping a cloth nearby to wipe the chin is one ordinary comfort they mention. Their examples of changes around teething are not a reason to assign every difficult spell to a tooth.
For newly emerged teeth, they describe cleaning with a soft cloth or toothbrush and water.
When crying is prolonged or a baby seems to be in pain, their broader care section describes sharing observations with a doctor or pediatrician and seeking medical advice.

references.locator: Variation between babies, wiping drool and care for newly emerged teeth
Observation, medical advice and adult support when crying or pain is concerning

ageContext.bookAge: The book gives no starting age for teething.
ageContext.readiness: For a tooth that has appeared, or a need for comfort; no tooth is expected at a particular age.

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
